questions.question: What manages computer hardware and software?
questions.explanation: Operating systems coordinate all computer resources.

questions.question: What type of software performs specific tasks?
questions.explanation: Applications help users complete specific tasks.

questions.question: What translates source code to machine code?
questions.explanation: Compilers convert code to executable form.

questions.question: What software protects against malware?
questions.explanation: Antivirus detects and removes threats.

questions.question: What allows hardware to communicate with OS?
questions.explanation: Drivers enable hardware-software communication.

questions.question: What software creates other software?
questions.explanation: Development tools help programmers write code.

questions.question: What improves system performance?
questions.explanation: Utilities optimize and maintain systems.

questions.question: What permanent software is embedded in hardware?
questions.explanation: Firmware provides low-level hardware control.

questions.question: What distributes software for free with source code?
questions.explanation: Open source allows code modification.

questions.question: What runs within another program?
questions.explanation: Plugins add functionality to host programs.

questions.question: Which of the following is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source operating system kernel; the others are applications.

questions.question: Which software translates and executes code line by line?
questions.explanation: Interpreters execute source code one statement at a time without producing a separate executable.

questions.question: Software that is free to use but whose source code remains closed is called what?
questions.explanation: Freeware costs nothing to use but remains proprietary, unlike open source software.

questions.question: Software distributed free for a trial period before purchase is called what?
questions.explanation: Shareware follows a try-before-you-buy model with a limited evaluation period.

questions.question: Which tool helps programmers find and fix errors in code?
questions.explanation: Debuggers let developers step through code, set breakpoints, and inspect variables to locate bugs.

questions.question: What type of malware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to unlock them?
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts files and holds them hostage until a ransom is paid.

questions.question: What software allows one physical machine to run multiple virtual machines?
questions.explanation: A hypervisor (or virtual machine monitor) allocates hardware resources among guest operating systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is application software?
questions.explanation: Excel performs user-facing spreadsheet tasks; the others are system-level software.

questions.question: What does GUI stand for?
questions.explanation: A GUI lets users interact through visual elements like windows, icons, and menus instead of text commands.

questions.question: Which type of program reduces file size to save disk space?
questions.explanation: Compression utilities like ZIP archivers encode data more efficiently to shrink file sizes.

questions.question: A program works on the developer's laptop but fails on the server because library versions differ. Which technology packages the app together with its dependencies to prevent this?
questions.explanation: Containers bundle the application with its libraries and runtime, so it runs identically on any host.

questions.question: In Git, which command creates a local copy of a remote repository on your machine?
questions.explanation: git clone downloads the full repository history to your machine; push uploads commits, commit saves changes, and merge combines branches.

questions.question: A team rolls a risky feature out to only 5% of users first, monitoring errors before a full release. What is this deployment strategy called?
questions.explanation: A canary release exposes changes to a small user subset first, limiting blast radius if something goes wrong.

questions.question: Why do teams use semantic versioning, such as labeling a release 2.4.1?
options: To signal whether a change is breaking, a feature, or a patch
questions.explanation: SemVer uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: bumping major signals breaking changes, minor adds features, and patch fixes bugs.

questions.question: A function crashes when a user submits malformed input. Which practice checks data at trust boundaries before processing it?
questions.explanation: Input validation rejects malformed or malicious data before it reaches business logic, preventing crashes and exploits.
